podcast.title: Subpop Singles Club (1988)
podcast.body: To enhance its appeal, Subpop launched the "Subpop Singles Club," which, for an annual fee, provided subscribers with a new limited edition seven-inch single every month. Nirvana's very first single was the inaugural release in November 1988. "And as an added touch, the company started the Subpop singles club for an annual fee. Subscribers received a brand new limited edition seven inch single in the mail every single month."

podcast.title: Hype Strategy for Grunge Bands - Early 1989
podcast.body: In early 1989, co-owners Jonathan Poe and Bruce Pabbitt, desperate to hype their acts like Nirvana, decided to emulate Jimi Hendrix's path to success by breaking bands in the UK first. Despite having no money, they risked flying a Melody Maker writer to Seattle to generate British press. "the two owners of the Subpop record label Jonathan Poe and Men and Bruce Pabbitt were desperate to hype their acts."

podcast.title: Cohesion for Seattle Underground
podcast.body: Despite being "terminally broke," Subpop provided a crucial sense of cohesion for the Seattle underground music scene, offering local acts a legitimate way to release material without compromising their punk credentials. "Although Subpop was terminally broke, the label nevertheless offered the Seattle Underground some kind of cohesion. Local acts now had a way of releasing material without jeopardizing their hard-earned punk credentials."
